subject: Sandbox-to-prod credentials, routing, and rerank integration playbook

Subject: Sandbox-to-prod creds & routing for embeddings/rerank demo

Hey Sean — great call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups from our side so we can move the PoC to a short POC next week:

Summary of ask
- We want to validate embeddings + rerank pipeline (client-side similarity + server-side reranker) against ~10M rows.
- We need a recommended auth approach for sandbox/dev vs production: we currently hand out basic API keys for dev but need a safer pattern for prod (rotation, least privilege).
- SDK quickstart: our mobile/web teams want a short path to call embeddings+rerank and then call structured tool outputs (we plan to call a payment-validate tool).
- Routing: can requests be pin-routed to cheaper quantized model for embeddings and higher-quality reranker for ranking?

Questions we need answered before next demo:
1) What credential pattern do you recommend for sandbox -> prod (API keys, service account, JWT/OAuth flow)?
2) Where to store/manage keys (we use AWS KMS + HashiVault) and what Redwood integrations exist?
3) Rotation: recommended TTLs and tooling to automate rotation?
4) Example SDK code for embeddings -> rerank -> structured tool calling (pseudo or short snippet is fine).

Next steps
- Can Redwood share a short checklist + recommended credential flows?
- We're available Wed 5/13 for a 30m technical walk-through with engineering (Alexa + myself).

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Sandbox-to-prod creds & routing for embeddings/rerank demo

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Posting a concise playbook below and attaching a one-page checklist (integration-checklist.xlsx). High-level recommendations first, then specific next steps and a link to a MAP (mutual action plan).

High-level credential pattern (recommended)
- Sandbox/dev: short-lived API keys with a strong prefix (e.g., sandbox_) and automated weekly rotation. Keys are fine for client SDK in sandbox if you guard them (rate-limit + domain/mobile app restrictions).
- Prod: server-side service account (longer-lived identity) that obtains short-lived JWTs for calls. Do NOT embed long-lived prod API keys in client apps. Use OAuth/JWT-based exchange (your backend -> Redwood token exchange).
- Ops & automation: store service-account private keys in Vault/KMS; Redwood supports verifying JWTs issued by your KMS-backed signing key (we can accept JWKS hosted in S3 or via your IdP).

Routing + model selection
- Yes — Redwood routing policies support model pinning per-route. We suggest: embeddings -> quantized emb model (cost-optimized), reranker -> high-precision model (higher perf tier). Routing can be done by endpoint configuration or dynamic request metadata (x-route-hint).

Rotation & TTLs
- Service account key: rotate every 90 days (automated via Vault).
- Short-lived JWTs: TTL 15m — issued by your backend on demand.
- Sandbox API keys: rotate 7–14 days.
- We provide webhooks for rotation events to invalidate caches on our side; recommend you consume those to keep stale keys out of circulation.

SDK snippets / tooling flow (very short)
- Step 1: obtain short-lived token from your backend (POST /auth/exchange -> {token})
- Step 2: call /v1/embeddings with Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Step 3: call /v1/rerank with same token and model=reranker-v2
- Step 4: call structured tool endpoint: include tool_call metadata in request and we will emit structured output you can parse.

Attachments & links
- integration-checklist.xlsx (attached) — quick items list for infra & app teams
- Mutual action plan (MAP): https://drive.redwood.ai/FinCo-Integration-MAP

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Ben will send a short technical checklist and a JWT flow diagram we can share with your infra team (by EOD tomorrow).
2) Schedule a 30m tech walk-through Wed 2026-05-13 10:00 PT — confirm if that works.
3) I’ll loop in Solutions Eng (Ben) to align on the SDK snippets and an initial test harness for the 10M rows sample.

Subject: Re: Sandbox-to-prod creds & routing for embeddings/rerank demo — technical checklist

Adding the technical checklist + a small diagram (jwt-flow-diagram.png) attached. Key points for your infra team to evaluate: 

1) Service account pattern (recommended prod flow)
- Create a Redwood service-account scoped to "embeddings:read, rerank:call, tools:invoke"
- Store the service-account private key in Vault (AWS KMS or HashiCorp).
- Backend exchange: your auth service signs a short-lived JWT (15m) for each session and posts to our /v1/token/exchange endpoint.

2) Minimal example (pseudo):
- Backend (Node):
  const jwt = sign({sub: "svc:finco-prod"}, PRIVATE_KEY, {alg: 'RS256', exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 900});
  const resp = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token/exchange', {method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({jwt})});
  const {access_token} = await resp.json();

- Client call:
  fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${access_token}`}, body: ...});

3) Rotation automation
- Recommended: use a HashiCorp key lifecycle job to generate a new RSA key pair, update JWKS, rotate any stored private keys, and call Redwood's rotation webhook to notify.
- Sandbox keys: use feature-flagged prefix and a scheduled lambda to auto-rotate every 7 days.

4) SDK bootstrap notes
- We have a lightweight SDK init: Redwood.init({env: 'sandbox', credential: {type: 'api_key', key: 'sandbox_xxx'}}) for quick testing. For production, SDK should call your backend auth endpoint to fetch access_token and set Authorization header.

5) Embeddings + rerank routing
- Use per-route model hints: "X-Model-Hint: embeddings-quant-v1" and "X-Model-Hint: reranker-high-v2". For higher throughput, batch embeddings with our streaming batch endpoint.

Attachments: jwt-flow-diagram.png

If helpful I can drop a tiny repo with the sample backend exchange by EOD. We should confirm your KMS choice (AWS KMS vs Google KMS) and whether you want Redwood to host JWKS or fetch from your IdP.

Ben Carter
